gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_775/slip: The focal slip reported a tally of six votes in favour, one against, and eight abstentions. This vote fell short of the required threshold for adoption. This outcome represented a separate amendment to the Brazilian draft, S/2023/775.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_775/matched: The Russian amendment to draft S/2023/773 inserted a paragraph after operative paragraph 2. It would have condemned indiscriminate attacks on civilians and civilian objects in Gaza, specifically referencing the strike on Al Ahli hospital without inferring a perpetrator. The text also proposed condemning blockade steps depriving the civilian population of essentials. The draft received six votes in favour, one against, and eight abstentions, falling short of the required threshold for adoption.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_776/slip: The focal slip reported a tally of seven votes in favour, one against, and seven abstentions. This resulted in a failure to reach the required number of votes. This was a separate amendment to the Brazilian draft.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.amendment_776/matched: The Russian proposal (S/2023/776) inserted an operative paragraph before paragraph 1 of the Brazilian draft. It called for a humanitarian ceasefire to begin immediately, endure, and be fully observed. The chair counted seven votes in favour, one against, and seven abstentions. This tally fell short of the required threshold, preventing adoption.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.draft_aid/slip: The focal slip reviews the proposed aid provisions within Brazil's draft S/2023/773. These provisions remained in draft language because the Security Council vote did not adopt the instrument. The negative vote of a permanent member prevented adoption, meaning the draft created no new Council authority.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.draft_aid/matched: The focal slip reviewed the proposed aid provisions of Brazil's S/2023/773. Operative paragraph 7 specifically proposed humanitarian pauses ensuring full, rapid, safe, and unhindered access for UN agencies, the ICRC, and other impartial organizations. It also encouraged corridors and aid-delivery initiatives. These provisions remained draft language because the Security Council vote did not adopt the instrument, preventing the creation of new Council authority.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.veto_explanation/slip: The U.S. representative stated that the United States voted against the draft because it failed to adequately address the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. This explanation concerns the main, vetoed draft only. The representative did not offer reasons for the abstentions by Russia and the United Kingdom.
gaza-2023-10-18-record-reconstruction.veto_explanation/matched: The amendment would have reaffirmed Israel's right of self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Speaking for the United States, Linda Thomas-Greenfield objected to the draft's omission of this right, arguing the Council should have explicitly included it in the text.
